ICSG PRESS RELEASE                                       Date Issued: 23rd November 2026 
 
Copper: Preliminary Data for September 2026 
The International Copper Study Group (ICSG) released preliminary data on world copper supply and demand for 
September in its November 2026 Copper Bulletin. The Bulletin and ICSG online statistical database provide data, on a 
country basis, for copper mine, smelter, refined, and semis production; copper refined usage; trade; stocks; and prices. 
The Bulletin is available for sale (annual subscription €600/€1200 for orders originating from/outside institutions based in ICSG member 
countries). 
Preliminary data indicates that world copper mine production declined by 0.9% in the first nine months of 2026, with a decline 
in concentrate production of 1.9% more than offsetting an increase in solvent extraction-electrowinning (SX-EW) of 2.7%. 
• Although global mine production benefited from additional output from projects ramping up to capacity in a number of countries, 
global growth was offset by important declines in concentrate production in Chile, D.R. Congo (DRC) and Indonesia. 
• Chilean production, that currently represents about 21% of world copper mine production, declined by 8% mainly as a result of 
reduced output at El Teniente, Escondida and Spence mines. Chilean concentrate production was down by 10.2% and SX-EW 
output remained essentially unchanged. 
• In Indonesia, concentrate production is estimated to have declined by 21% as output at the Grasberg mine remains constrained by 
the impact of a severe mud rush incident that occurred in September 2025.  
• Mine production in the DRC is estimated to have remained unchanged: growth of about 5% in SX-EW output has been offset by a 
23% decline in concentrate production, due to reduced output at Kamoa mine (impact of a seismic event in 2025). 
• In Peru, copper mine production remained essentially unchanged: significantly higher production at Antamina (+36%) was offset by 
a decline in output at other major mines (Las Bambas, Antapaccay, Southern Peru Copper, Quellaveco, Cerro Verde, Toromocho 
and Marcobre).  
• Mongolian copper concentrate has grown by about 20% as a consequence of the Oyu Tolgoy UG project ramp-up; Australian mine 
output is estimated to have declined by 10% mainly due to the closure of Mount Isa mine in July 2025. 
Preliminary data indicate that world refined copper production grew by about 1.4% in the first nine months of 2026, with primary 
production (electrolytic and electrowinning from ores) growing by 0.9% and secondary production (from scrap) increasing by 3.8%. 
• Production in China and the DRC, which currently represent about 59% of global production, is estimated to have increased by a 
combined 3.6% (China 3.3% and DRC 5%). World refined copper output excluding these two countries declined by about 1.6%. 
• Chilean refined copper production declined by 7%, with electrolytic production (from concentrates) down by 21.5%, impacted by 
smelter operational constraints and maintenance, and electrowinning (SX-EW) remaining essentially unchanged. 
• Output in Asia (ex-China) is estimated to have declined by 1%, as lower output in Japan, Indonesia and the Philippines offset growth 
in other Asian countries. Production in India is estimated to have increased by 25% due to improved operating capacity rates. 
• Global secondary refined production (from scrap) increased by 3.8% mainly due to growth in China. 
Preliminary data suggests that world apparent refined copper usage increased by 1% in the first nine months of 2026. 
• World ex-China usage is estimated to have declined by 0.4%, and Chinese apparent demand (excluding changes in 
bonded/unreported stocks) is estimated to have increased by 2%. Chinese net refined copper imports declined by 14%. 
• China's share of total world refined copper usage is currently about 59%. 
Preliminary world refined copper balance indicates an apparent surplus of 222,000 t in the first nine months of 2026. 
• In developing its global market balance, ICSG uses an apparent demand calculation for China that does not consider changes in 
unreported stocks (State Reserve Bureau (SRB), producer, consumer, merchant/trader, bonded). To facilitate global market 
analysis, however, an additional line item - Refined World Balance Adjusted for Chinese Bonded Stock Changes - is included in the 
attached table that adjusts the world refined copper balance based on an average estimate of changes in bonded inventories 
provided by two consultants with expertise in China’s copper market. 
• In the first nine months of 2026, the world refined copper balance, based on Chinese apparent usage (excluding changes in 
bonded/unreported stocks), indicated a preliminary surplus of about 222,000 t. This compares with a surplus of about 127,000 t in 
the same period of 2025. The world refined copper balance adjusted for estimated changes in Chinese bonded stocks suggested 
a market surplus of about 185,000 t. 
Copper Prices and Stocks: 
• Based on the average of estimates provided by two independent consultants, China’s bonded stocks are thought to have declined 
by about 37,000 t in the first nine months of 2026 compared to the year-end 2025 level. 
• As of the end of October 2026, copper stocks held at the major metal exchanges (LME, COMEX, SHFE) totalled 1,068,086 t (highest 
level since May 2003). Stocks increased by 323,971 t (+43%) compared with stocks held at the end of December 2025, and were 
up at the LME (+148,450 t) and COMEX (+276,251 t) and down at SHFE (-100,730 t) 
• The average LME cash price for October was US$ 14,532.48 /t, up 0.3% from the September average US$ 14,483.39 /t. The 2026 
high and low copper prices until 20th November were US$ 14,850 /t (on 17th August) and US$ 11,826 /t (on 19th March), respectively, 
and the year-to-date average is US$ 13,552.75 /t (+36.3% above the 2025 annual average). 
(World Refined Copper Usage and Supply Trends table on next page) 
Please visit the ICSG website www.icsg.org for further copper market-related information.
